name: NGC 266 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 266, a barred spiral galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc266-hubble
story: Hubble returned to the place in this galaxy where the supernova SN 2005gl exploded. The star that died there was likely a luminous blue variable, a rare ultra-bright kind that theory says should not explode so early, and Hubble later saw that it was gone.

claims.text: SN 2005gl was a Type IIn supernova in the galaxy NGC 266
NGC 266 is a barred spiral galaxy
The progenitor was a rare class of ultra-bright star that, according to theory, shouldn't explode so early
The very massive progenitor star was likely a luminous blue variable
Later Hubble imaging showed the progenitor star was gone
Program 14115 imaged supernova sites to confirm progenitor candidates; target SN2005GL
